title: PixelKin - The Three Hours (set-piece battle bed)
_note: The shared legendary-triad battle bed (walkthrough/07-the-three §3.6: boss register, but AWED, not heroic — you are fighting a keeper of the sky's turning, and it is letting you). Devices: 3/4 like a GREAT CLOCK under the music at 76 BPM; a low tri_bass PENDULUM swinging root-fifth-root every bar (the jammed wheel, still rocking); sparse BELL hour-marks (one toll every two bars — midnight is the hour no bell marks, so the bell never completes a peal); a PATIENT minor lead built on the Vesper rising-leap contour (E4→A4→B4 lift-overshoot, then the stepwise settle) over three 8-bar strophes whose cadences RESOLVE ONE CHORD FURTHER EACH TIME — strophe 1 hangs on the minor v (Em), strophe 2 falls deceptively to bVI (F), strophe 3 finally reaches the harmonic-minor dominant (E, G# leading tone) and the loop seam hands it home to Am: the wheel turns one notch per strophe and never quite completes, because completing it is the player's job. Strings carry the chords in the o3 pad register (snes band convention); drums are a soft clock (tom tick on 1, hat on 2-3), never a battle kit. A minor, 24 bars of 3/4 (~57s loop), peak 7 voices. era snes, rendered on the chip engine for cohesion. Original melody throughout (VISION.md).
key: A minor (harmonic-minor dominant at the seam)

tracks.name: lead
tracks._note: Patient, long-breathed, chord-anchored — the Vesper lift-overshoot-settle contour opens each strophe a little higher and lands a little further. Strophe 1 (bars 1-8) hangs unresolved on B (the v). Strophe 2 (9-16) reaches higher and falls to A over the deceptive F. Strophe 3 (17-24) crests at E5, touches the G# leading tone, and leaves B4 hanging into the seam, where the bass lands Am.

tracks.name: bass
tracks._note: THE PENDULUM — root-fifth-root quarter notes, one swing per bar, never syncopated, never resting: the great clock under the music. Chords: Am Am F G Am Dm Em Em | Am C F G Dm F G F | Am F C G Dm Am E E.

tracks.name: hourmarks
tracks._note: Sparse hour-marks: ONE toll every two bars, on the downbeat, ringing the bar out — an unfinished peal (A E A B / A C B A / E C D E... never a scale, never a tune; the hours being counted, not sung). Silence is the other half of the part.

tracks.name: strings
tracks._note: The vastness — one smooth-voiced triad per bar in the o3 pad register, full-bar dotted halves, voice-led so the top line barely moves (a sky, not a riff). Same progression as the bass pendulum.

tracks.name: drums
tracks._note: The clock, not a kit: a low tom tick on beat 1, soft hats on 2 and 3, every bar identical — time passing under the fight. A single crash marks each strophe's first bar (the hour changing).
